correctness.rationale: The claim is correct for candidate sites, not actual poles. Independently, dividing the reciprocal sextic by X^3 gives g(Y)=Y^3-5Y-6 with Y=X+1/X. The cubic has no rational root, has discriminant -472 and one real root Y>2, and the norm of Y^2-4 in its cubic field is g(2)g(-2)=32, not a rational square. This supplies irreducibility of the sextic without relying on the finite checker. The plus-sqrt(2) cubic has the positive root in (0,1), hence the other two roots u and conjugate(u) have product alpha. Irreducibility of this cubic over Q(sqrt(2)) follows from the sextic degree and the cubic equation; an embedding taking u to alpha^-1 disproves torsion of u/conjugate(u) by the modulus of its image. Exponentiating the fundamental-strip representative gives the product of the five conjugate ratios exactly, so equality of sites is equality of the ordered pairs, including on the strip boundary. The two unit coordinate columns give all pairs starting with (0,0); summing the five independent geometric factors gives the bivariate and diagonal series. The pole of the diagonal series at t=1 has leading part 1/[36(1-t)^5] and other poles have orders at most two, yielding the stated leading coefficient and average.
